title: Hiyu Yamakoshi Season Review: 'A positive surprise' after multiple podiums in 2026
excerpt:
Hiyu Yamakoshi's debut FIA Formula 3 campaign was 'better than expected' according to the Japanese driver.

He earned a maiden pole position and multiple podiums across the 2026 season, results he had hoped for but not expected prior to the year getting underway.

Reflecting on the season overall, Yamakoshi says that things had gone well and he'd surprised himself at points.

"I think it's like 9 out of 10, I'd say. Most of the things I achieved I didn't expect before the season, especially after the first round.

"We had a three-month break and we learned a lot, we improved a lot from Monaco all the way to the end. For me, the results were way more than what we expected."

Looking at what went well, the Van Amersfoort Racing driver says he and the team adapated well during the extended break in the year following Melbourne.

He says that they returned to Monte Carlo with a better understanding of how to optimise races, and throughout the heart of the season in Europe, he was able to achieve strong results.

"I think I understood the F3 car quite a lot during the break. I was obviously always thinking during the race about tyre management, how to manage our position with tyre strategy, the track conditions, the track temperatures. Everything like that is information that's really crucial.

"That makes it different from what I've done last year. The strongest weekend was definitely Barcelona. My first time in the top three in the championship after the disqualification in the Monaco Sprint Race.

"We gained a lot, I think it was around 23 or something points. It was very crucial at that stage in the championship as well. So I'd say Barcelona.

READ MORE

Brando Badoer's Season Review: Highlight moments and bouncing back from tough rookie year

Ernesto Rivera Season Review: Mental resilience, pure speed and more to come

Yamakoshi secured podiums in Monte Carlo until disqualification took that result away, but then responded immediately in Barcelona with P2 in the Feature Race. He added a pole position to his 2026 record at Red Bull Ring, before returning to the podium in Spa.

Third in the Monza Sprint Race was his final rostrum visit of the campaign, but he says he was surprised to be competing at the sharp end so often, impressing himself in the process.

"I expected I could fight in the sprint races, top three all the time. But I really didn't expect I could fight in the Feature Race for the win.

"I think I've fought for the win four times in Barcelona, Spa, Red Bull Ring and Monza. But still, I really didn't expect it. Everything was more than what we expected. The team was really impressed me and I impressed myself as well."

Overall, Yamakoshi's campaign was successful enough that he is now competing with VAR in FIA Formula 2, debuting at Round 12 of the season in Baku.

He will be aiming to hit the ground running in the step up, something that he says impacted his campaign in F3 earlier in the year.

"I'd say race management is what I learned the most. That's what happened in Barcelona, Spa. Got DRS before it was too late and managed the position when we wanted to.

"Qualifying is always difficult, it's all about how we can put in a lap. It's more about how much the driver can do. But in the race, it's more about how we can manage the position and how we can manage the tyres.

"I think that's my strong point. But the big lesson this year is from the start of the season. We were really fast in testing, always in the top 10. But suddenly, in Melbourne, we're P20. Not the team, but for myself, I'm P22.

"My team-mates are P11, P12, and so we lost many points. I think the potential is that we could have got 10 points at least from that weekend."

title: Brando Badoer's Season Review: Highlight moments and bouncing back from tough rookie year
excerpt:
Brando Badoer is delighted with how well he bounced back from his rookie season to put in a stronger campaign with Rodin Motorsport in 2026.

The Italian driver ended the year seventh in the Championship after a 2025 campaign where he finished 25th in the Standings.

Speaking at the finale in Madrid, Badoer spoke with the pride at the season he has put together this year.

“It's definitely been a good season overall,” he said. “Lots of good races, important races and memories with the team. Of course, we got the Monaco win, and we got four podiums, and we worked really well throughout the year.

“Coming into the last round we were a couple of points off P3 in the championship, in the top five. It was a really good fight for it so definitely a strong season overall.

“I think overall we had a lot of positive things. Some things we could have done better. Every year when you look back at the season, there are a lot of things where you think I lost points there or there. But it's normal and it's that way for everyone.

Badoer finished eighth in the Standings after ending up 25th in 2025

“Sometimes we got good luck, sometimes bad luck. But overall I can be happy about the work I've done in F3, and I'm really thankful for every part of the team, the mechanics, engineers, the team manager, for all the work they've done alongside me.”

When asked what he felt he had improved upon this year compared to 2025, Badoer responded: “I'm definitely happy to have shown the world my potential. The worst season was last year.

“I usually always perform at a high level, but last year for many reasons it was impossible. Definitely tough moments make you stronger.

“So I would say the determination, motivation and the support of my team made it possible. People forget about a negative 2025, which was definitely a tough one to deal with.”

Badoer concedes that consistency was something he improved on this year even if it was not always perfect, as he acknowledged that Formula 3 is a “difficult championship to be always competitive in”.

Badoer praised Rodin for their work with him this season

But that didn’t change the 20-year-old’s approach, who believes his hard work was the biggest strength this season.

“Maybe it might sound a bit obvious, but I would say the hard work,” said Badoer when asked about his biggest strength in 2026. “Going into every tiny detail when things are not as good as they should.

When asked to pick a highlight moment, Badoer said: “Winning in Monaco. I've had many good moments, but for sure that stands out.

“I think I achieved it, and it was a good celebration. It was a good celebration, but not long because I had Barcelona.”

title: Ernesto Rivera Season Review: Mental resilience, pure speed and more to come
excerpt:
While it was hardly the start Ernesto Rivera would have been hoping for in 2026, seventh in his rookie FIA Formula 3 campaign capped off a positive year for the Mexican driver.

Driving for Campos Racing and helping the Spanish outfit to a second consecutive Teams' Championship and was vying for a top three finish in the Drivers' Standings in his own right.

A difficult final round in Madrid proved costly, but that hardly detracts from what was a very impressive debut in the Championship.

His season started on the worst note possible as injury ahead of pre-season testing left him facing an uphill struggle and behind his rivals in terms of preparation.

"I think it has gone really well, for sure better than what I expected and probably what most people expected," Rivera explained.

"I missed the start the season because of the back injury and also missed the pre-season test. But since Monaco I've been on it honestly. For sure I've made some mistakes and lost some points but I think it's been a really good rookie campaign."

Going into depth on the struggles he endured in the early months of the season, Rivera explained that it was a challenge mentally as well as physically.

"I was having a tough campaign in New Zealand, in the Formula Regional Oceania, and yeah honestly I just wanted to get back to Europe and start with the test in F3 and with Campos.

Rivera started 2026 on the back foot but quickly made up for lost time

"It was tough having the injury in the last race of the championship in New Zealand. I ended up having to go to Mexico, and in that first week, I was only able to walk, not do anything else and I was just sitting there watching the times of the test and yeah, it was tough mentally the first week.

"After that I just said to myself there's nothing you can do, just try to treat the recovery as positively as possible and let's see if you can come back to Melbourne.

"We decided I couldn't race in Melbourne because I was not even going to the gym yet, I still had a lot of pain.

"I lost a lot of muscle. I was like six kilos lighter because of the muscle loss, so it was tough to be as prepared as possible for Monaco."

Pedro Clerot returns with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season

When he did get in the F3 car, he delivered instantly. P5 on Feature Race debut around the streets of Monte Carlo underlined his potential, and the 2026 season only grew from there for Rivera.

Three races later, he was standing on the top step of an F3 podium for the first time, victor of the Spielberg Sprint Race and the strong start caught the Campos driver by surprise also.

"I thought I could do good, not as good as I've done honestly. I didn't have such high expectations, but yeah I think I made a lot of progress. I've tried to work really hard and improve in all the areas as possible.

The Red Bull Junior Team Driver says he was proud to achieve multiple wins with Campos this year

"Qualifying, I've always been there, but maybe the races I've struggled a bit more with tyre deg and I've been improving quite a lot. I hope to carry these learnings for the rest of my career."

After the Sprint win, the next target was a Feature Race victory, and he didn't have to wait long. It arrived around the circuit he rates as his favourite on the calendar, and it was arguably his most complete drive in the Championship.

Rivera says it was a showcase of his learnings across the season, from tyre and race management to wheel-to-wheel battling and working with his team.

"For sure winning in Spa is my highlight. It's my favourite track of Europe and I did a great race. The car was great, tyre management was great and yeah, overall it was a good weekend. It's where I gained a lot of points, climbed the standings with that win and I think that is the highlight of the season."

After a challenging campaign, with setbacks, peaks and highlight moments, Rivera says that there are plenty of takeaways from the 2026 campaign. The biggest point however is self-belief.

"I've got to trust myself more. Sometimes last year I wasn't so confident in myself and after this year, I know that I can do it.

"I think it has helped me a lot, for my confidence, I think that's where I improved a lot away from the driving side of things. I started to trust myself more and handle those pressure scenarios better."

title: Pedro Clerot returns with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Rodin Motorsport has confirmed that Pedro Clerot will continue with the team for a second season in FIA Formula 3 in 2027.

Clerot had a strong rookie campaign with Rodin, finishing sixth in the Drivers' Championship helped by his five podiums – which include a Feature Race 1 victory at the final round in Madrid.

Prior to that, the 19-year-old won the 2022 Brazilian F4 title and finished fourth in the 2025 Formula Regional European Championship.

Clerot is now set to return for a second season in Formula 3, and the Brazilian driver expressed his delight at being able to do so in an environment where he feels very comfortable.

“I’m very happy to be staying with Rodin for my second year in FIA F3,” said Clerot. “We’ve built a really strong relationship this season and achieved some great results, improving race after race. I’ve felt at home with the team since day one, so continuing this journey together is very special.

“I believe we have what it takes to fight at the front next season, and I’m excited to see what we can achieve together.”

Rodin Motorsport Sporting Director Benn Huntingford added: “We’re delighted to continue our relationship with Pedro for another season in FIA Formula 3. He’s really impressed the team this year, showing strong pace and making great progress throughout the season. To see him take his maiden win in Madrid was a fantastic way to end the year and a result that reflects the progress he’s made. We’re looking forward to building on that next season and seeing what we can achieve together.”

title: TRIDENT confirm the signing of Kean Nakamura-Berta for the 2027 season
excerpt:
TRIDENT have announced the signing of Kean Nakamura-Berta for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 campaign – the first confirmed driver for the upcoming season.

Having made the step up from karting in 2023, Nakamura-Berta boasts an impressive record in single seaters having won 2025 Italian F4 and E4 Championships titles.

In 2026, the Williams Driver Academy member won Formula Regional Middle East Trophy title, and he also finished third in the Formula Regional European Championship.

Nakamura-Berta is now set to graduate to Formula 3 in 2027, and at the announcement, he expressed his delight at the opportunity to race with TRIDENT.

“I’m pleased to be stepping up to F3 with TRIDENT Motorsport while still having the ongoing support of the Williams F1 Team Driver Academy,” said Nakamura-Berta.

“Finishing the season strongly in FREC and having the opportunity to join such a competitive team in F3 gives me great confidence as I look ahead to my F3 debut next year. A big thank you to everyone involved who helped get me here.”

TRIDENT Team Manager Giacomo Ricci added: “We are extremely pleased to announce the arrival of Kean Nakamura-Berta at TRIDENT Motorsport for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship season. Kean is a driver we have known and followed for some time, and he has demonstrated he has all the qualities needed to take this important step. His journey, from karting to Formula Regional, has been marked by constant growth and impressive results. It will be a pleasure to begin this collaboration and work together to best prepare for such an important campaign. We are convinced that Trident represents the ideal environment to allow Kean to continue his growth and express his full potential in the FIA Formula 3 series.”

Williams F1 Team Sporting Director Sven Smeets also added: “It's a proud moment to see Kean step up to F3 with Trident Motorsport for his rookie season. He has made impressive progress since joining the Academy this year, and this opportunity is a culmination of the hard work and dedication he's shown across a long and hard-fought title campaign, backed by an already outstanding record. This is a great moment for the Driver Academy, and a fitting reflection of the opportunities it creates for the next generation of talented drivers.”

title: Clerot reflects on ‘really special’ Madrid weekend after claiming maiden victory
excerpt:
Pedro Clerot was pleased to bring a very “successful season” to a close with a special performance in Madrid – the Brazilian claiming his maiden Formula 3 victory in Feature Race 1.

The Rodin Motorsport driver was impressive at the Madring circuit, missing out on pole position by 0.012s in Qualifying 1 on Friday.

Clerot was then in the fight for pole on his final lap in Qualifying 2 but hit the barrier at the last corner and settled for third place.

The Brazilian driver then made a great start from P2 in Feature Race 1 to take the lead and the victory before adding another podium to his weekend tally with a P3 in Sunday’s race.

Speaking on his way out of the paddock with his two trophies in hand, Clerot reflected on a strong few days in the Spanish capital.

Clerot achieved his maiden win in Formula 3 in dominant style in Feature Race 1

“It was a really special, really special weekend,” he said. “It is really good to finally show what we had, maybe I'd say the whole year in terms of pace.

“Obviously, I'm not going to say luck was on our side, we did the work, we put a lot there in qualifying and we had a very good start yesterday.

“It's a very successful rookie season, some coulda, woulda, shouldas out there, but I’m just very happy to end the season like this.”

title: Taponen reflects on ‘satisfying’ end to the season after victory in Madrid
excerpt:
Tuukka Taponen claimed his maiden FIA Formula 3 victory in the Madrid Feature Race 2 – and that earned him third place in the Drivers’ Championship.

The MP Motorsport driver had a great final round, finishing third in Qualifying 1 and taking pole position in Qualifying 2.

Taponen would convert that into a podium in Feature Race 1 and held off champion Ugo Ugochukwu in Feature Race 2 to take the victory.

Speaking at the end of the weekend, the Finnish driver says staying ahead of his Campos Racing rival was vital to the victory.

“It was a good start,” said Taponen. “I thought about it last night that I really want to focus on the start. I wanted to make sure I was ready.

“Everyone starting on the grid knew that was crucial because overtaking is difficult later on. It was a good start, and after that, I controlled and managed the race. I picked up the pace when needed. In the end, I built up a gap to Ugo.

title: ‘We’ve been incredible all season’ says Slater as he reflects on 2026 campaign and title loss
excerpt:
Freddie Slater admitted he was gutted to have not fought for the title in the way he wanted in Madrid. But he also paid tribute to rival Ugo Ugochukwu, Campos Racing and his team TRIDENT.

The British driver went into the weekend with a 15-point lead over Ugochukwu in the Standings, but was 17th in Qualifying 1 and eighth in Qualifying 2 after dealing with an issue on his car.

Ugochukwu, on the other hand, was fourth and second, and on a track where it is tough to overtake, Slater could not do much to catch up with his rival in all three races.

Both drivers were tied going into Sunday’s final Feature Race, and with Ugochukwu second and Slater seventh, the American took the title.

Reflecting on it all afterwards, Slater said: “Obviously a little bit gutted with the end result, but fundamentally we had too many things go wrong. The Feature Race in Monza, that was the start of it, and then this weekend in qualifying we had too many issues.

“On a track like this it's very difficult to overtake as well, so when you're at the back or in the mid-pack it's always going to be difficult. To be fair, fair play to Ugo and Campos, they had a good weekend.

Slater struggled in Qualfying in Madrid as he and TRIDENT struggled with an issue

“But we didn't really get the fight we wanted with the issues we had but overall it doesn't detract from the season we've had.

“We've done an amazing job all year to be a rookie with the performances we've had, we’ve been incredible all year. So it's just a shame that sometimes motorsport is like that, but that's how it is sometimes.”

Reflecting on the season as a whole, Slater had one win, three pole positions and eight podiums in total. Despite it not leading to the title, he views the year with a huge amount of positivity.

“I think as a rookie, trying to gain the experience and get on level with the second-year drivers as quick as I could has been really well managed,” he said.

“The pace has been incredible all year, very consistent, and executed all the time. Unfortunately there's some variables that went the wrong way out of our control, and those affect the results.

“They came at the worst possible time if I'm honest, because obviously there's no time now to catch up, it's over. So a little bit gutted the way we couldn't really finish the job off and really fight for it and show what we have been all season.

Slater's 2027 plans are already set as he will race in Formula 2 with Invicta Racing

“But it doesn't take away what we've done all year. We've done an amazing job, and I couldn't have done that without my team, TRIDENT. So a massive thank you to them.”

Slater’s 2027 plans have already been announced as he will step up to FIA Formula 2 with Invicta Racing. His goal now is to make sure he is ready for the challenges that lie ahead.

“We’ve still been fighting for another championship,” he continued. "It's another year done and another championship nearly won. So it's been an impressive career so far.

“But now there's some exciting things hopefully to come in the future. Still a steep hill to climb, that's for sure. So I need to continue to keep pushing and try and develop into a better driver, that's the aim of the game.

“So we're going to have a nice off-season, mostly with friends and family, and relax a little bit. But also get ready for next year to see what that holds.”

title: ‘This was my main goal’ says Ugochukwu after sealing Formula 3 title in Madrid
excerpt:
Ugo Ugochukwu is the 2026 Drivers’ Champion, completing what he believes has been the best season of his career to date.

The Campos Racing driver went into Sunday’s Feature Race 2 tied on points with Freddie Slater, and by finishing second, compared to his rival in eighth, he claimed the title.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, a delighted Ugochukwu spoke of the importance of winning this championship.

“I'm feeling really good, for sure,” said Ugochukwu. “This was the main goal at the start of the year, to get the championship.

“I think after quali we knew we did our job, we did the main task, and today, and yesterday, it was just about execution and getting the points and bringing it home.

“There was a little bit of pressure which is pretty normal. This last weekend was definitely the most important one of the championship, with two Features.

Ugochukwu kept things calm and controlled out on track on his way to the title in Madrid

“So, quali was pressure to get the job done. I thought I performed with the pressure, I had the right risk versus reward and didn't make any mistakes. Ultimately today, we benefited off the good quali.

“Today I knew what I had to do to win the championship. So, it was in my hands to keep it clean, keep the cars behind at bay, and just bring it home to the line.”

This result represented a massive turnaround for Ugochukwu as he went into Sunday’s Feature Race in Monza starting at the back of the field, while Slater went from pole.

But with his rival not finishing and him making a comeback to the points, he set himself up for a title showdown in Madrid.

Speaking about his mentality through it all, Ugochukwu said: “I think coming into this weekend, we were quite fortunate to be able to come in 15 points behind.

Ugochukwu is Campos Racing's first FIA Formula 3 Drivers' Champion

“We used that to our advantage. 15 points is still a decent gap, but I knew that was enough to put a bit of pressure on our rivals, and ultimately, we managed to perfect this last weekend, execute it well, and that's what gave us the championship.”

Reflecting more on his season long battle with Slater, Ugochukwu says it was one he enjoyed.

“It was a great battle throughout the year and we really enjoyed it,” he said. “I think beginning of the year, we knew from testing and Round 1 that it might be us two at the end that we would be battling for the championship.

“But to come down like that, to the wire, with equal points in the last race was pretty crazy. So just obviously really happy to get it done and to clinch the title and to come out on top.”

Looking back on the year, Ugochukwu started 2026 winning the Formula Regional Oceania Championship in New Zealand ahead of Slater.

Ugochukwu achieved the goal he set out to at the beginning of the season

The 19-year-old ranks this season as the best of his career to date.

“I think this year is probably one of my top ones of my racing journey, my racing career, 2026 as a whole,” added Ugochukwu.

“Really happy that I've been able to show what I can do. Two titles this year this being my second, and for sure this is the one I really, really wanted to get done.

title: Thoughts of a Champion - Ugo Ugochukwu
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Welcome, everyone, to the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Champions Press Conference. Many congratulations to our FIA Formula 3 Champion, driving for Campos Racing, Ugo Ugochukwu. Ugo, congratulations. You were locked in a tight battle with Freddie Slater all season. What was your mindset coming here to Madrid with such a close championship battle?

Ugo Ugochukwu: For sure, I was not expecting to come into the final race equal on points, but it made it very exciting. I think we did a good job all weekend. We put ourselves in a good position after qualifying and in the races, so today was just about executing and doing our job properly. P2 was not a bad result. I was just trying to manage my tyres. We knew that was what I needed to win the championship, so it was just about getting it home.

FIA Formula 3: Two victories and seven podiums. You have had a lot of great moments, but is there one moment in the season that stands out for you?

Ugochukwu: I think there are a few. For sure, round one in Melbourne was super special. That was my first win in Formula 3 and it gave me a lot of confidence to continue pushing throughout the season, knowing that we were in the championship fight. Monza was also important, coming back to score a few points. We were fortunate to come into this weekend only 15 points behind, and that really allowed us to apply pressure, attack and ultimately take the championship.

FIA Formula 3: You came back for a second season after a tough rookie year. How much have you learned and matured since stepping into the Formula 3 paddock, and how proud are you of the level of performance you have shown this year?

Ugochukwu: I am super happy. Overall, I think I have improved and evolved as a driver. That is also my goal for the following years, to keep performing better and better. This title is a testament to that, so I am really happy with the work we have put in with the team. I am super happy for them as well, clinching the Teams’ Championship yesterday, and today we got the job done to seal both. It has been pretty much a perfect season for us.

FIA Formula 3: You led the Drivers’ Championship for much of the season, but was there any point when you doubted your title hopes?

Ugochukwu: I would not say I doubted, but there were definitely some points when it looked like we had lost the advantage and needed to come back a little bit. I always kept the faith that I would be able to do it. I had a lot of confidence coming into this weekend, despite being 15 points behind, and I knew it was still possible. We executed everything well, and that allowed us to get the job done.

FIA Formula 3: You are Campos Racing’s first FIA Formula 3 Champion. What does that mean to you, and how key have they been to your success this season?

Ugochukwu: It is super special. The whole team is very happy with this. Our goal at the beginning of the year was to fight for the championship, and that is what we have done. We managed to come out on top, so I cannot thank each and every one of them enough for all their hard work. We have worked well together since before the season started, and I think that really paid off. Starting the championship well is always important, and we finished the season well this weekend too. I am really happy to clinch this first title for Campos.

FIA Formula 3: What is next for the FIA Formula 3 Champion?

Ugochukwu: We will see. Formula 2 is, of course, the next logical step up the ladder towards everyone’s dream of Formula 1. For now, I am just enjoying this title and this championship. The whole of 2026 has been very good for me, winning two championships, and we will see what 2027 brings.

title: Round 9 Post-Feature Race 2 Thoughts from the Top Three
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Tuukka Taponen, from pole position to first at the flag, your first win of the 2026 season. It was the last race of the season, but that must still be a great moment for you?

Tuukka Taponen: Yes, these last three weekends have been super good for us. We were really struggling earlier this season and it was not looking so good, to be honest. But we have done such a good job and worked so much to improve our performance. I think the results speak for themselves. It has been a super end to the year.

FIA Formula 3: Can we talk about the race today? You started from pole position alongside the not-yet FIA Formula 3 champion, Ugo Ugochukwu. In yesterday's races, every time, P2 became P1 at the first corner. Did you have that in mind when the lights went out?

Taponen: It was on my mind already last night when I was going to sleep. It was really stressful because I knew it needed to be a clean, good start. There was no need to do anything special, just make a decent start and it would be enough. That is what we did and we managed to stay ahead.

FIA Formula 3: Towards the final laps, Ugo came closer and was putting pressure on you. Was it a different kind of pressure knowing that he had everything at stake? Were you a little more relaxed seeing him behind you?

Taponen: I knew Ugo's situation. I was pretty sure he was not going to attack me. I was managing at the front and controlling the gap behind. Then I was going to push a little more at the end to get the fastest lap, which I did on the final lap. I was just keeping it on track and driving smoothly.

FIA Formula 3: At the end of the day, this is P3 in the 2026 standings for you. Knowing how difficult your season has been, are you happy with that finishing position?

Taponen: Yes, after everything we have had, I am super happy. I could not believe this a few weekends ago. I was far from P3, but it has been super close in this championship from P3 to around P10. I knew everything was possible here, especially with two Feature Races. Qualifying was key because overtaking is very difficult. I am super happy with how the season finished.

FIA Formula 3: Are your 2027 plans already set, or were you waiting for that final result before thinking about them?

Taponen: For me, it is a difficult situation. I do not have a place for next year. Struggling with the financial side is part of motorsport, but we are trying our best to do something next year. I hope we can make a decision soon.

FIA Formula 3: Thank you very much, Tuukka. An excellent job this weekend and best of luck for the future. Ugo Ugochukwu, you came into this morning at Madrid in P2, with your title rival having scored zero points yesterday and starting P8 behind you. Did you feel relaxed coming into the race, or are you never relaxed when you know you are racing for the championship?

Ugo Ugochukwu: It is hard. In a way, I knew I was in a good position to get the championship today and I knew what I needed to do to win the title, but I was not fully relaxed. You think about all the little things that can happen and that you need to stay on top of. Today was executed quite well. I knew I had a good chance on the inside to maybe go for the lead at the start, but Tuukka did a good job defending his position. From there, it felt like a very long race. I just had to manage the tyre and the gap to the drivers behind me. That is what we did. To win the championship is testament to the consistency and the job we have done throughout the year.

FIA Formula 3: Yesterday we saw three races, two Formula 3 races and one Formula 2 race, and every time P2 was leading into Turn 1. Were you playing it safer than anything else, simply wanting a clean start?

Ugochukwu: For sure, a clean start was on our minds. We could not afford a stall, a jump start or anything like that. Getting into the lead at the start would still have been nice because controlling from the front is always a little easier and cleaner, but I knew I just had to adapt to whatever situation I was in. Whether that was P2 or P3, I just managed the race as best as I could. I tried to make a move later on and put on a bit of pressure, but Tuukka was quick in the right places and I could not get quite close enough. Qualifying was the key to this weekend and we executed that well to put ourselves in a good position today on such a tricky track.

FIA Formula 3: With all the pressure and what was potentially waiting at the end, was that the most difficult race of the season for you?

Ugochukwu: It definitely was one of the most difficult races. In terms of performance, we were quick and I did not have too much pressure from behind, but at the same time you cannot afford any mistakes with such a big thing on the line. I made sure to keep it clean. We have seen a lot of damage to the cars from the kerbs here throughout the weekend and in testing as well, so I tried to be gentle with the car and make sure it reached the line.

FIA Formula 3: There was one final Safety Car period at the end and one final lap of racing. During that Safety Car period, did you think it was done, or did you wait until the chequered flag before you could really let it all go?

Ugochukwu: Initially, I thought it was going to end under the Safety Car because I saw there was no work being done on the car. My engineer also thought it was going to be over, but then he came on the radio and said there would be one more lap. I started working on my tyres again to be fully prepared for that lap. I held my breath for one lap, and once I crossed the line I could relax a little.

FIA Formula 3: From all of us at FIA Formula 3, huge congratulations on a great 2026 season. We look forward to seeing what you do next. Pedro Clerot, P3 in today's final Feature Race of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship. It is another podium after your win yesterday in the first Feature Race. What an amazing weekend you have had. How are you feeling right now?

Pedro Clerot: Very good. It was obviously a very strong weekend on our side, both for me and the team. I am very happy that we could end the season on a high. As I said before, it was a very tough year for us, but to finish like this makes it extra special. I am very happy with the work we put in after the test and also Monza. We knew coming here that we had a good chance to fight, but I try not to think about results and just focus on the work. That is what we did and that is what we achieved. Yesterday was a very good race, winning and controlling it completely. Today, we brought home good points for both the Teams' and Drivers' Championships. I am obviously very happy. Maybe we could have fought for a little more, but I will take it. After such a hard year, it is good to finish like this.

FIA Formula 3: This was your rookie season in Formula 3. What did you learn from your first season in this championship? We know it is one of the most competitive championships out there.

Clerot: For sure. You do not get much driving in this series. It is all about adapting and being in control of the things you can control. I am very happy with what we achieved. Five podiums this season is something I never imagined doing in my rookie season. We always aim to fight for the championship. It was not to be this time, but I am very happy with the work we did with Rodin this year. I have learned a lot. Rodin have been like a family to me this year and welcomed me very well from day one, so I am very happy with what we achieved. Hopefully, I can get some more silverware in whatever comes next.

FIA Formula 3: The end of the season always brings questions about what is next. You will not reveal your plans, but do you already know them, and are you happy with them?

Clerot: Yes, I am very happy with how the plans look for next year. Obviously, I cannot share them, but it is going to be very nice. I am very happy to be going where I am going. I think it is going to be a very strong year. We have the capability to fight for championships in whatever comes next. I am looking forward to it, but I also want to enjoy some free time now, spend time with my family, go back home to Brazil and celebrate a little.

FIA Formula 3: Good job on your first season, Pedro, and best of luck for what comes next.

title: Brando Badoer: ‘Top 3 the target’ as he analyses F3 season so far

title: Surpassing expectations and targets to hit: Hiyu Yamakoshi on his 2026 season so far
excerpt:
It has been an impressive rookie season from Hiyu Yamakoshi. The Van Amersfoort Racing driver has secured two podium finishes already this year alongside a pole position, and is hoping to return to the rostrum before the season is out.

The Japanese driver admits that his fast start to the campaign surprised even him, but that he has had a shift in mentality in the subsequent rounds, and is aiming ever higher.

"I really didn't expect to get in a pole position in Red Bull Ring. A podium was expected at some point, but not in the Feature Race. I expected I'd have some podiums in the Sprints, but actually my first podium was in Barcelona, P2. Actually, we were chasing P1 all the way.

"It was really, really good. For me, I think I made very good progress from last year and from the past few years. Those results really have given me extra confidence going into every race weekend.

"For me, the biggest thing for my mentality is that I realised I'm not slow. I can compete with the top drivers, the top F1 junior team drivers. I can compete with them, actually I can fight with them, actually I'm sometimes faster than them. That really makes me extra confident.

Yamakoshi is part of a VAR team that has one driver in their second year and another rookie alongside him. Bruno Del Pino has brought his learnings from 2025, while Deligny has been a solid benchmark to rate Yamakoshi against so far this year.

Yamakoshi was particularly happy with his Barcelona weekend and fight for victory

For the Japanese driver, it has been a combination that's worked well and brought strong results across the board for the team. All three have been on the podium this season, and for Yamakoshi, it has been a benefit to learn from both, as has an environment at VAR he already feels at home within.

"Obviously Enzo is a rookie, same as me, learning as much as we can from Bruno. In the first few rounds, I learned a lot from Bruno, and the team really helped me to put me in the top 10, top 12 all the time.

"That really helped particularly with tyres. Even from F4, I had different engineers every year telling me, the one thing you need is to be really good in tyre management, which is really crucial in F3 and F2.

"I think the familiarity is really helpful. For me, I know everybody from F4. Of course engineers are different, mechanics are different, but I know them, they know me, and they trust me. That's the reason why stayed with VAR in F3.

"I think also braking, technique-wise, I can brake hard but nicely, complimenting my driving style."

The VAR driver is aiming for a return to the podium in the final races

With two rounds remaining and three Feature Races, Yamakoshi is clear he is aiming for a return to the podium before the final chequered flag of 2026.

That's something he feels is well within range should he and VAR maximise their Fridays at Monza and Madrid, with a top 12 in Qualifying the target.

He will be using the break as a time to reset and not think about racing too much in order to be fully rested and ready for the final two rounds.

"I want to get some more podiums. From my mentality side, even on the race weekend, when I'm back to the hotel, I'm completely off from racing. So basically for my summer break, I'll just take a break as much as I can, chill away from racing, but not gaining any weight, don't eat too much, obviously! But for me, the most important thing is during the break, just rest as much as I can.

"If we can have good qualifying results, we have more chances to win. So, let's see. For me, I have really good confidence."

title: Mixed so far but optimistic for the final double-header: Noah Stromsted on his F3 season so far
excerpt:
Noah Stromsted sits sixth in the FIA Formula 3 Drivers' Championship after what has been a mixed year up to this stage.

The Dane has stood on the top step of the podium following a great drive in Spielberg, but other moments have limited his scoring potential.

Reflecting on the campaign to date ahead of the summer break, the TRIDENT driver explains where he's struggled and why he's optimistic going into the final races of 2026.

"It started out quite tough this year, I have to say, with penalties and a bit of performance," he admitted. "But I think from the midway point, we made a good step and from there, we've been fighting at the front where we should be.

"Looking at Spielberg, we had a very good car from the start there and then everything becomes easier just building on that. You don't have to think so much about what to do with the car and it's just about focusing on driving.

"I think at some tracks, we've been starting out on the wrong foot, I would say. Then, I've been doing some mistakes driving myself also. So just a combination of that.

"I think when you have a better understanding of everything before driving, you know what to expect more or less. So that makes it easier. You start with the car in the window and then can focus on maximising the driving."

After that win around the Red Bull Ring and a great haul of points the following weekend at Silverstone, the final two rounds prior to the break did not go to plan.

It left Stromsted outside of the top five in the Standings, with two points across the four races. He says that the break comes at a good time for him to reset ahead of a vital double-header that takes the Championship to Monza and then Madrid.

"Spa in the end - the qualifying was okay before the penalty for both races, then it becomes a bit tougher. For some reason, we're lacking quite a bit of race pace, which normally we have been quite strong.

READ MORE

‘Improvements across the board’ and aiming to end on a high: Bruno del Pino on his F3 season so far

"I think it's good to have a bit of a break. We've been on it since Monaco. So I think it'll be good to have a break and just get away a bit and try to understand and be ready for the last two rounds.

"I still have quite a bit of sim in between then and now. So I wouldn't call it a full break. But it's just a bit more time at home and a bit more relaxing, but still working on the sim and preparing."

Drivers will head to the Madring prior to racing resuming at Monza for a vital two-day test around the new venue.

Stromsted is optimistic he can get back into a good run of form before the end of the season

Stromsted says that the test will be pivotal with nobody knowing what to expect and the test will give everyone the chance to learn in the real world as opposed to the simulator.

After that however, all bets are off, with the typically chaotic Monza Qualifying session and a double-Feature Race finale in Madrid.

The TRIDENT driver says he'll remain focused on himself throughout rather than setting a points goal.

"I think it's very useful for us. Of course, nobody knows the track and to go there without any knowledge, it's very difficult. That's even more true with the double Feature Race schedule we have, where there's a lot of points at stake, so it's very good to have the test before.

"Monza - I'm expecting a quite chaotic weekend, to be honest. A bit like last year, the races are very fun, but the qualifying will be, I think, a big mess, like the last couple of years. I mean, we'll take what we can from there, but I think it'll be a difficult weekend.

"In the end, it's just focusing on myself, focusing on where we can get the performance and on driving, and then see in the end in Madrid where we end up. Of course, I'm quite a few points behind first and second, so if we're to fight for those positions, I think something needs to happen. You never know though."

title: ‘Improvements across the board’ and aiming to end on a high: Bruno del Pino on his F3 season so far
excerpt:
It has been an up and down season for Bruno Del Pino so far in 2026, with the Van Amersfoort Racing driver flying out the gates but then experiencing a tougher period.

The Spaniard sits ninth in the Standings, 10 points adrift of P6 going into the final two rounds, and believes he can return to the podium and finish on a high note.

Ahead of the summer break, the VAR driver went into depth analysing his season so far, and what to expect when racing returns in Monza.

"I think we can take many positives,” he stated. “I think we've shown that we are very strong, we've shown that we can be up there.

"The last three rounds, many factors, from my side and external factors have also impacted things, but I think even with that, we've shown that we could fight up there.

"We still have two rounds to go and it will still be positive overall if we put things together, which I think we will. So, I'm happy with the job done so far, I'm happy with myself and I think we can still continue to go on and get good results before the end of the year."

Del Pino remains optimistic that he can get his season back on track and finish higher in the order, having been in and around the top five in the Standings for much of the early phase of the year.

It has been a tough phase of the season but Del Pino is confident he and VAR can end the year strongly

"I had been top five for basically the entire season. I demonstrated that I was there, it’s just been these last few rounds that went off course. 10 points from sixth and I think even fifth is within reach. It's doable and I'm very positive that we can get the job done.”

The summer break comes ahead of the final two rounds and for the Spaniard, he says it could have come sooner. But, he will be taking the chance to reset himself and prepare as much as possible for the final double-header of the year.

That of course includes a finale and pair of Feature Races in his home city of Madrid. Del Pino says it could make all the difference as he will be feeling the support around him that weekend.

"I mean, if it was me, it could have come after Barcelona or Spielberg when things started to go south a bit.

"It's a good moment to have a break. We've been non-stop racing and going back to the factory for so many weeks, I think sometimes you need a bit of a recharge.

“Of course, if I could drive a car every day of the year, I'll drive a car. But, it's also good to relax a bit, reflect upon what went well, what didn't and reset for the last two and a half rounds.

The Spaniard says his F3 experience has helped in his second campaign

"We're going to do the best we can to achieve everything that is possible and keep on with the progress because every race is a way to outdo yourself. And I think we can do a really good job, as we've shown, and try to finish the championship in style and with maximising everything.

"I had a special edition helmet in Barcelona. I think I'm going to present a new one in Madrid, which is very special. I live in Madrid, it's the city my father was born in.

Kato keen to return to the podium before seasons end after ‘unlucky’ run of form

“It's great, finishing the season there, being able to go and relax at your house every single day, get all your family and friends together to the last dance. Because you never know what's going to happen next year.”

Del Pino is in his second year of FIA Formula 3, and says he feels he has made great strides since his rookie campaign in 2025.

The Spaniard says he is a ‘more complete driver’ in comparison to the one that debuted in the Championship over a year ago now, but that there’s still things he and his team can improve in the final rounds of this season to end on a high.

A return to the podium is the target before the end of the 2026 campaign

"It's just been more complete, being more under control of what I can achieve. Of course, with many more points, it also motivates me, knowing that I've been working as hard as I can to do it.

“My position in the championship has improved, so overall, I think it has been a big, big improvement. Coming into F3, you're fighting against top drivers at this stage of their careers, so it's obviously very difficult.

“So that year of experience has also helped me a lot, especially in the beginning of the year where I knew what to expect on the new tracks that maybe some rookies didn't expect."

“It's very important for me because you're in a moment in your career where F2 is right there, and then you look to F1. The window is getting very small. So every option - it's more limited every year that goes by.

"So I will be trying to finish the season in the best possible way, with all the support from family and friends which will be really, really important for me."

title: Shining bright on the big stage and helping out a close friend: Freddie Slater on his 2026 helmet design
excerpt:
Freddie Slater gives us the down low on his 2026 helmet design

Championship leader Freddie Slater heads into the summer break top of the FIA Formula 3 pile, but he took time out ahead of the holidays to talk us through his 2026 helmet design.

Featuring the Audi rings for the first time and maintaining what has been a signature look since karts, the TRIDENT driver dives into the design and how it came about.

"This has always been my style. I've always had an 'F' somewhere in my helmet on the side since karting, and it's always been there, just changing colours over the years a little bit.

"This year we decided to go with a bit more chrome to get a bit more of a sparkle effect. The addition of the four rings is very special as well on the 2026 helmet. It fits very well with the TRIDENT colours, so it all came together.

"Miles Murphy of MDM Designs, they've always done all my helmets since I started racing cars. Bell provide the helmet as well. I wouldn't have any other provider if I'm honest. They're a great bunch of people and create amazing helmets, so it's very special this one. Best on the grid, no bias at all.

READ MORE

Kato keen to return to the podium before seasons end after ‘unlucky’ run of form

"In terms of process, It's quite tricky with helmets because you want to get something that reflects you and is your style. Obviously year after year there's more designs being used, so it's quite hard to come up with something new.

"You also want to keep a little bit of what you normally have. I've had this sort of style since I started really, and that's why we try and keep it year by year. So that's always the goal.

"I had a special one this year for Silverstone, it was more of a pure blue. Blue is my favourite colour, it suited the design very well. We added lots of chrome sparkles. It was a one-off helmet for Silverstone, but I wouldn't be surprised if we see it back out again at some track soon. Maybe another special event or whatever comes up.

"I've got the Team Will sticker on the top of my helmet. Will McIntyre is going through such a difficult period in his life and nobody ever wants to see that. Much love to all the family and our support goes out to them.

"The racing paddock has all come together to unite and support him. He's got some amazing charity events, which we need to get as many people to.

"He's fighting against Neuro XLP1 which requires a stem cell treatment, so anybody that's able to can get involved via his website. I just want to help one of my closest friends.

"We started in karts together and we've always been on a journey together. It's obviously made me very proud and happy to help him as much as I can. So please get involved there if you can.

"In terms of the design overall, I think this year for my favourite part is the chrome and the 'F'. It's always been part of my design. I like the chrome that makes it shine a little bit more on track.

"It looks great in the photos, especially when the lighting is nice. Now the addition of the four rings is even more special."

Next Up

title: Kato keen to return to the podium before seasons end after ‘unlucky’ run of form
excerpt:
Taito Kato has been reflecting on his debut Formula 3 season – looking at the positives and negatives from the 2026 campaign.

The ART Grand Prix driver’s season got off to a great start finishing third at the opening race weekend at the Melbourne Feature Race.

But in the six rounds since, Kato has finished in the points just six times and has not yet returned to the rostrum.

Going into the summer break, the Japanese driver is now down to 12th in the Drivers’ Standings with 45 points. While the results have not been what he wanted, he sees some positives from his season.

“I think I have been able to adjust quite well to Formula 3,” he said. “There's obviously not so much track time in Formula 3. In FRECA, there was much more on track time. We had two FPs and then two qualifyings.

Kato is 12th in the Drivers' Standings with 45 points after a mixed bag of results

“But Formula 3 is always 40 minutes Practice, and then one qualifying. So, it’s the biggest difference, but even with not so much on track time, I have adjusted quite well. On the track I have been driving for the first time in places like Melbourne, Monaco, and Silverstone.

“I'm not so experienced myself, but I have adjusted quite well myself. So I think that is my strongest point.”

WHAT WE LEARNED: Some of the key takeaways from Round 7 in Budapest

Kato has made a name for himself this season for pulling off daring overtaking moves in the midfield.

However, if you ask him, it’s something the Japanese rookie would rather not do.

“I think during the race, the battles, the wheel-to-wheel I'm really strong,” he said. “I am able to make big moves, so that is my strong point.

Kato is happy with how he has adapted to Formula 3 with ART

“But to be honest, I don't like battles so much. I want to win from first position and drive alone. But it is how it is, that’s racing. It's impossible to do P1 to P1 everytime in Formula 3, it’s always difficult.

Kato heads into the final two rounds after a point-less outing in Budapest, but he still has desires on making it back into the podium before the season’s end.

“It is a new track, so we have some data, which is quite good. We are doing a lot of preparation for the race weekend, and we have had a lot of meetings. I think everything was correct. Everything was really great. The preparation is almost perfect.

“We need a bit more preparation during the race weekend just to make sure we are ready to fight for the race weekend. We want to fight for the podium and also hopefully get some wins. But for sure, my target is a consistent result in qualifying.

“I want to make sure we are inside the top 12. If you are inside the top 12, you have some good opportunities in both races. So make sure you are consistent in the qualifying and then you can fight for the podium and for the victory. That is my goal for this season.”

title: Pedro Clerot on his rookie F3 campaign, improvements and why winning is 'a matter of time'
excerpt:
Pedro Clerot has been enjoying an impressive season as a rookie in FIA Formula 3. The Brazilian driver has taken three podiums already with Rodin Motorsport, sits 10th in the Drivers' Standings and is closing in on a first victory in the Championship.

With the summer break now upon us, he looked back at what he'd accomplished so far, talked in depth about his thoughts on the year so far and where the areas of improvement are.

"We can be satisfied with what we've done," Clerot explained. "It's been a little bit on the inconsistent side, but I think as a rookie and with Rodin, we've built a good relationship so far and we've been doing a good job, especially the last few rounds.

"I'm happy and enjoying my racing and I think it's been a decent rookie season so far. As drivers we aim to be fighting for the championship, even though you are a rookie.

"But being close to Brando, a second-year driver, and scoring some decent points are results that we can be proud of. I think we could be a bit further up, but still we've been doing a decent job."

Having secured podiums in Monte Carlo, Spielberg and Spa, the Rodin driver now has his sights set on a maiden win in F3, something he says is 'a matter of time.'

Based on his speed and wheel-to-wheel prowess so far in 2026, you wouldn't bet against him. He says that there's proof in his results he has what it takes to make that final step in performance and achieve that goal before the end of the season.

"We're fighting guys like Ernesto and some good second-year guys as well. To be fighting with the top teams and the top drivers even though I'm a rookie proves we can be up there.

"I think the win is a matter of time, honestly. It hasn't come yet, but it's a matter of time. I've been working a lot lately, especially the last few weeks to try to make it happen.

"If we just put our head down, work hard, we can achieve some good results. I'm just focused on doing my job, trying to maximise every little bit and I think in doing that the win is a matter of time. Things will come together and I'm sure it will happen soon."

Still, he's hopeful that in the final two rounds of the season, and with another Qualifying session in Madrid to contend with, he and his team can show their true potential over a flying lap and therefore giving himself a great chance of more positive results.

"I wouldn't even say it's a one-lap issue. I think we've been very unlucky. We had the brake issue in Melbourne, which completely ruined our Qualifying and we had a really strong Free Practice, being P7. I think we had for sure the pace to be inside the top 12.

"Monaco, we had a good Qualifying, nothing to say there, but then heading into Barcelona we had a couple of issues also that were out of mine and the team's control. "Obviously, the aim and the target is always to be fighting in the top five. That's my goal, but I'm just focused on doing my job race by race and it should come together."

title: Bruno Michel’s Spa-Francorchamps and Budapest Debrief
excerpt:
After all of the action from Spa-Francorchamps and Budapest, the FIA Formula 3 campaign is nearing the final stages of what has been a thrilling title fight.

Freddie Slater took over at the top after his maiden victory in the Championship around the Hungaroring, while Ugo Ugochukwu will want to overturn the narrow deficit come Monza.

Giving us his take on the action we’ve seen ahead of the summer break, FIA Formula 3 CEO Bruno Michel reviews and gives his thoughts on the latest chapter of the season.

A NEW WINNER AT SPA

“It was a very good race weekend. Spa is always a quite demanding track and it's very interesting.

“The Sprint Race was good, we had a new race winner, Jin Nakamura, and he did a very good race. It’s good to see Hitech back in the picture because they had not been there for a while. So, all together, it was good.

“Nakamura drove a clean race, got his overtakes done when he needed to and showed great control once he was into clean air and at the front of the pack.

READ MORE

‘We push each other’ – Ugochukwu reflects on 2026 title fight with Freddie Slater

“In the Feature, we had another winner, Ernesto Rivera, and he did a fantastic race. It’s a shame that he missed the first race weekend of the Championship due to injury, because now he's fighting at the front. He's a strong driver, Campos is doing very, very well and he's up there with his teammates.

“He isn’t far off teammate Théophile Nael in the Standings, now just three points back from third place in the Standings. The Mexican driver has hit a great run of form heading into the final rounds and looks to be improving every weekend as he makes up for his delayed start to the 2026 campaign.”

THE TITLE FIGHTERS

Rivera has been impressing as the season has gone on, with the rookie taking his maiden Feature Race win at Spa

“In terms of the Championship, because Ugo had a difficult weekend in Belgium, he didn't score points, while Freddie was on pole, didn't win, but he's on the podium again.

“Campos remain the team to beat, quite a bit ahead of TRIDENT. Let's see if they can catch up, but Campos has got a solid edge in the Championship at the moment.

“Freddie Slater finally won a race at the Hungaroring, and at the perfect time. I must say, he had a very, very strong race on Sunday, and now he's leading the Championship.

“Ugo has been very, very strong as well in Hungary. He started from P6, overtook quite a few cars, and there was a great fight between the two at the top of the Championship, so it's getting extremely exciting.

“It's very difficult to know who will come out on top. Freddie is now going to have more confidence because he's done a very strong job in Budapest, but Ugo is strong, and he's a great racer. So, let's see.”

SUMMER BREAK AND WHAT COMES NEXT

Slater finally got his F3 victory and with it, took over at the top of the Drivers' Standings

“We head into the summer break after a thrilling couple of rounds that has helped shape an already exciting title battle between Freddie and Ugo.

“I have no doubt they will both have more highlight moments in the races to come, and whoever comes out on top will be a worthy Champion in the end.

“Next up we go to Monza, a circuit that always delivers thrilling racing no matter what, and we’ve seen time and time again how title fights can change lap by lap and even corner by corner.

“Then, we go to the Madring for the first time. Teams will have a test there ahead of the race weekend in what will be a vital two-days of track time.

“There’s an extra Feature Race for the ninth and final round of the season, so there is still plenty of points to play for. Let’s see who comes out on top!”
